anti_overlap: Do not analyze walk pacing as physical exercise or distance optimization — that is the falconry/fly-fishing lens
Do not analyze rare/common probability curves as statistical distributions — that is the mushroom-foraging lens
Do not analyze the ethics of leaving something for later — that is the gleaning lens
Focus only on the architecture of a single ceremonial event and how density preserves or destroys that architecture
decision_lens: Does this density option preserve the architecture-of-approach that makes a single encounter feel like the destination of the walk, rather than one event among many? Is the threshold-crossing legible to the player?
distance_rationale: A 400-year-refined ritual practice from a non-Western contemplative tradition has no semantic overlap with mobile game design, but its central concern — compressing meaning into a single host-guest encounter — is structurally identical to what Unc Rancher needs each Unc meeting to feel like
expected_isomorphisms: The roji-to-tearoom approach maps to the GPS walk-to-encounter transition; the hanging scroll maps to the chosen lure media; the 3-beat dialog maps to the calibrated sequence of bowl-preparation gestures; ichigo-ichie maps directly to 'we respect our Uncs'; the question 'how many tea ceremonies per afternoon?' has a 400-year answer (one, with a meal-included chaji running 4 hours; the shorter chakai is also typically one per occasion) that bears directly on Options A vs C
focus: Encounter as ceremonial compression — the architecture of approach, threshold, and single guest-host event
name: fd-chanoyu-approach-architecture
persona: Apply the perspective of a chanoyu (Japanese tea ceremony) master in the Urasenke tradition — they care about the deliberate compression of attention into a single guest-host encounter, the calibrated stages of approach (roji garden → crouching entrance → hanging scroll → bowl), and the way scarcity of moments is what gives each its weight.
review_areas: Whether each density option has a clear roji equivalent — a transitional walking phase that prepares the player for the encounter
Whether multiple encounters per walk dilute the host-guest reciprocity that makes the 3-beat dialog feel earned
Whether the lure functions as a hanging scroll (a chosen object that focuses the encounter's meaning) or becomes a vending-machine token
Whether 'nothing today' walks (Option D) preserve ichigo-ichie ('one time, one meeting') by making the meeting non-guaranteed
Whether the ranch home-screen is read as a tokonoma (alcove for contemplation) or a trophy shelf, and how density shapes which
Whether the 60-90 second encounter has enough ceremonial stages internally to bear the weight density places on it

severity_examples.condition: If density exceeds one ceremonial focal point per session, each encounter loses the architectural weight a 3-beat dialog needs to land — the dialog becomes interaction-rate friction rather than focused meeting
If the wildcard arrives without its own approach-phase (no walking-time threshold, no tonal preparation), it breaks the chanoyu structure that the primary encounter establishes

source_domain: Chanoyu (Japanese tea ceremony), specifically the Urasenke tradition and the principle of ichigo-ichie
success_hints: Map each density option to a roji/threshold/tokonoma equivalent and call out which option has no analogue
Distinguish between scarcity-of-encounter (rare meetings) and density-of-attention-within-encounter (depth of one meeting) — chanoyu shows these are different axes
Cite ichigo-ichie as the principle and explain when it fails (when meetings become routine)
Note that the host prepares; the guest arrives — who is the host in Unc Rancher, and does density change that role-asymmetry?
task_context: Review encounter-density options A/B/C/D for Unc Rancher v0 with a chanoyu-trained eye on the architecture of approach and the ceremonial weight of a single meeting.
